_**Legend of Mana**_[[Note 2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legend_of_Mana#cite_note-Title-2) is a 1999 [action role-playing game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Action_role-playing_game "Action role-playing game") developed and published by [Square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Square_(video_game_company) "Square (video game company)") for the [PlayStation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_(console) "PlayStation (console)"). It is a [spin-off](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spinoff_(media) "Spinoff (media)") of the _[Mana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mana\_(series) "Mana (series)")_ series. Set in a [high fantasy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High_fantasy "High fantasy") universe, the game follows an unnamed hero as they restore the land of Fa'Diel by creating the world around them and completing a number of interrelated [quests](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quest_(video_gaming) "Quest (video gaming)") in order to restore the Tree of Mana.

While incorporating [action role-playing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Action_role-playing_game "Action role-playing game") elements from the prior games in the series, such as [real-time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turns,_rounds_and_time-keeping_systems_in_games#Real-time "Turns, rounds and time-keeping systems in games") battles, _Legend of Mana_ has its own distinct style of gameplay. Most notably, it gives the player the ability to shape the world's structure through the Land Make system, generating regions and quests in a [non-linear gameplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nonlinear_gameplay "Nonlinear gameplay") system rather than a strong main plotline. _Legend of Mana_ was directed by series creator [Koichi Ishii](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koichi_Ishii "Koichi Ishii"), designed by [Akihiko Matsui](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akihiko_Matsui "Akihiko Matsui"), and produced by veteran Square director and producer [Akitoshi Kawazu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akitoshi_Kawazu "Akitoshi Kawazu").

The game had high sales, selling 400,000 copies in its first week of release and 700,000 by the end of 1999. Reviews were less positive than for prior games in the series. Critics gave considerable acclaim to its vibrant and colorful hand-drawn graphics and soundtrack by Yoko Shimomura, but were critical of the lack of a clear main storyline, stating that it left the game feeling disjointed. The game was re-released as a part of both the PlayStation's and Square's best-sellers lines. It was released as a PSOne Classic in Japan and North America. A remastered version was published by [Square Enix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Square_Enix "Square Enix") for the [Nintendo Switch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nintendo_Switch "Nintendo Switch"), [PlayStation 4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_4 "PlayStation 4") and [Windows](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windows "Windows") on June 24, 2021, for [Android](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Android_(operating_system) "Android (operating system)") and [iOS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IOS "IOS") on December 7, 2021, and for [Xbox Series X/S](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_Series_X_and_Series_S "Xbox Series X and Series S") on September 26, 2024. An [anime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anime "Anime") adaptation by [Yokohama Animation Laboratory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yokohama_Animation_Laboratory "Yokohama Animation Laboratory") and [Graphinica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graphinica "Graphinica") titled _[Legend of Mana: The Teardrop Crystal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legend\_of\_Mana:\_The\_Teardrop\_Crystal "Legend of Mana: The Teardrop Crystal")_ aired from October to December 2022.

## Gameplay

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Legend_of_Mana&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Gameplay")]

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/a/a6/Legend_of_Mana_battle.jpg/250px-Legend_of_Mana_battle.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Legend_of_Mana_battle.jpg)

A boss battle featuring the protagonist and a Rabite pet. The party's [health](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Health_(gaming) "Health (gaming)") and special move meter is shown in the gauges at the top, and the enemy's health is shown in the bar at the bottom.

Like previous games in the [_Mana_ series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mana_(series) "Mana (series)"), _Legend of Mana_ displays an angled [top-down perspective](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Video_game_graphics#Top-down_perspective "Video game graphics"), in which the [player characters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Player_character "Player character") navigate the terrain and fight off hostile creatures. The player controls the unnamed main character, and is assisted by up to two companions. One of these companions is an optional support character, which depends on what [quest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quest_(video_gaming) "Quest (video gaming)") the player is performing, while another companion can be chosen by the player out of a roster of monsters, pets, and [golems](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golem "Golem"). Both companions are typically controlled by the game's [AI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_intelligence "Artificial intelligence"), though a second player can take control of the support character, or load in their own character from a different save file, if present.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legend_of_Mana#cite_note-EGMpreview-3) The main character and companions each have their own set of numerical attributes including [hit points](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Health_(gaming) "Health (gaming)") and strength, which represent the amount of damage the player can take or cause. These stats grow whenever the player advances a level, after gaining enough [experience points](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Experience_point "Experience point") from battle with enemies.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legend_of_Mana#cite_note-RPGamer-4)

Battles occur when the player character encounters an enemy while traversing the world. Combat takes place in real-time, and in the location the player found the enemy rather than a separate battle screen. The main character can equip a variety of weapons, armors, and accessories. Weapons let the player perform abilities in combat. Referred to as Special Techs, these abilities are powerful attacks by the main characters and support characters that can be used when the special move meter is full. This meter fills as the player damages enemies. Each weapon, such as a sword or spear, has a set number of special attacks to learn, which can hit single or multiple targets and can be assigned to different buttons on the controller.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legend_of_Mana#cite_note-RPGamer-4)

_Legend of Mana_, unlike previous games in the Mana series, does not feature a set journey through a fixed world. Instead, it features a unique "Land Make" system where the player generates the structure of the game world by placing objects, named Artifacts, on empty square plots on a map. This map takes the form of a grid of spaces presented in an [isometric](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isometric_projection "Isometric projection") viewpoint on a map screen. When an Artifact is placed in a space on the map, it creates a Land, and the player can enter that Land by selecting the position on the map. Adjacent Lands are not connected; to move from one land to another the player must first return to the map screen. Different Lands are generated from different Artifacts, each containing a quest which upon completion usually gives the player another Artifact to place.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legend_of_Mana#cite_note-GameSpotReview-5) Lands can also contain additional quests. Each Land is ranked from 0 (no presence) to 3 (strong presence) in its strength in each [Spirit of Mana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mana_(series)#Common_elements "Mana (series)"); this in turn causes magic of that element to be stronger in that Land.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legend_of_Mana#cite_note-GamePro-6) The strength of the rankings is dependent on the Artifact, its position on the Map, and the rankings of adjacent Lands. Many locations have [non-player characters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-player_character "Non-player character") who give quests and information or sell equipment. Other areas feature enemies and [bosses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boss_(video_gaming) "Boss (video gaming)") with which the player can battle.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legend_of_Mana#cite_note-EGMpreview-3)

In addition to the main game, after certain quests are completed _Legend of Mana_ gives the player the option to delve into optional gameplay aspects centered around the hero or heroine's house. The player can [forge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blacksmith "Blacksmith") or improve weapons and armor using raw materials found throughout the game, or combine equipment with items to change their power or add special effects. They can grow different types of fruit in the orchard, raise pets to use as adventuring companions, create items, and build golems.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legend_of_Mana#cite_note-GamePro-6) Pets can also be raised with the Japan-only [PocketStation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PocketStation "PocketStation") peripheral, and two players can battle each other in an arena.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legend_of_Mana#cite_note-pocket-7)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legend_of_Mana#cite_note-arena-8)

## Plot

### Setting

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Legend_of_Mana&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Setting")]

_Legend of Mana_ is set in the fictional world of Fa'Diel. The Mana Tree, the giver of mana and life for the world, burned down almost entirely nine centuries prior to the events of the game. A war erupted between faeries, human, and others seeking the scarce power of mana that was left. When the war concluded, the burnt Mana Tree slept as it regrew and the many lands of the world were stored in ancient artifacts.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legend_of_Mana#cite_note-QuoteIntro-9) A hero, controlled by the player, is self-charged with restoring the world, and mana, to its former self. The Lands of Fa'Diel are populated with a large number of different creatures, including humans, faeries, demons, the [jewel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gemstone "Gemstone")-hearted Jumi race, plant-like Sproutlings and Flowerlings, [miner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mining "Mining") bears called Dudbears, and shadowy beings of the Underworld known as Shadoles. Fa'Diel is also the home of a host of [anthropomorphic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthropomorphism "Anthropomorphism") animals and objects, as well as monsters from other _Mana_ titles such as Rabites, Chobin Hoods, and Goblins. The player controls the protagonist of the game, who is either a male or female [silent protagonist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silent_protagonist "Silent protagonist"). The character is unnamed and no information is given about their past; their history and personality is meant to be determined by the player.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legend_of_Mana#cite_note-ultimania-10)

### Characters and story branches

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Legend_of_Mana&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Characters and story branches")]

Rather than a single, overarching plot, the story of _Legend of Mana_ is composed of a multitude of quests split into three main quest arcs, numerous other quests, and a final quest arc. Each main quest arc contains optional side-quests in addition to the main quests. Whenever the player completes the required portions of one of the quest arcs they are allowed to begin the final arc and finish the game, even if the other arcs have not yet been started or completed. The three main quest arcs prior to the final arc are: the Jumi arc, the Larc and Sierra arc, and the Matilda and Irwin arc.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legend_of_Mana#cite_note-RPGamerEd-11)

The first main arc is the story of the Jumi, a dying race of people who have external jewel hearts which are considered valuable. The Jumi have long been a persecuted people, and many magic characters in this game refer to them as "dirt" as a pejorative on their jewel cores. This branch focuses on Elazul and Pearl, who are among the few survivors of the Jumi. Elazul is a Jumi Knight, and the mission of his life is to protect the Jumi Guardian Pearl at any cost, even in the face of the jewel hunter, Sandra. The player assists them in helping the Jumi.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legend_of_Mana#cite_note-QuoteJumi1-12)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legend_of_Mana#cite_note-QuoteJumi2-13)

The second arc is the story of Larc and Sierra—brother and sister dragoons who serve different dragon masters and fight on opposite sides of the same war for power. Larc serves the dragon Drakonis, who wants to kill the other three dragons so that he can rule the world. Larc blackmails the game's protagonist to help him in this quest. Sierra, a dragoon for Vadise the White Dragon, wants to stop Drakonis without hurting her brother Larc. In the end, Drakonis is defeated again and banished to the underworld, and Larc is freed from Drakonis' rule.

The third arc is the complicated love story of four childhood friends: Matilda, Irwin, Daena and Escad. Irwin is a half-demon who is angry that society prevents him from a relationship with the holy leader Matilda, and seeks to destroy the world in retribution. Escad seeks to destroy Irwin, and Daena tries to act as a [mediator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mediation "Mediation") between all parties while keeping Matilda away from Irwin. The conflict eventually escalates into a war between humans and [faeries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fairy "Fairy"). Depending on the choices of the player, either Daena or Escad will die, while the player helps bring an end to the conflict.

Regardless of which path(s) the hero decides to take, they begin the game's final story, titled "Legend of Mana". This arc concerns the re-appearance of the Mana Tree. The player journeys to the Mana Tree and scales it, but upon reaching the top they find that the Mana Goddess has become corrupted and the tree is rotten. The player is forced to fight the Mana Goddess, and after winning a Sproutling plants itself in the Mana Tree's rotten trunk. Calling upon the other Sproutlings to join them, they restore the Mana Tree.

## Development and release

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Legend_of_Mana&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Development and release")]

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/ae/Akitoshi_Kawazu_%282007%29.jpg/250px-Akitoshi_Kawazu_%282007%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Akitoshi_Kawazu_(2007).jpg)

Producer [Akitoshi Kawazu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akitoshi_Kawazu "Akitoshi Kawazu")

_Legend of Mana_ was directed by [_Mana_ series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mana_(series) "Mana (series)") creator [Koichi Ishii](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koichi_Ishii "Koichi Ishii"), who had worked on the three previous games in the series. Many of the other developers were new to the series, including producer [Akitoshi Kawazu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akitoshi_Kawazu "Akitoshi Kawazu"), the director and producer of many games in Square's _[SaGa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SaGa\_(series) "SaGa (series)")_ series, and designer [Akihiko Matsui](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akihiko_Matsui "Akihiko Matsui"), who had been the director for _[Chrono Trigger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrono\_Trigger "Chrono Trigger")_. The game's character designs and illustrations were done by Shinichi Kameoka. _[Retro Gamer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retro\_Gamer "Retro Gamer")_, in 2011, stated that although Ishii kept the game tied to previous titles in the series by reusing gameplay elements, Kawazu had a heavy influence on the gameplay design of the game.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legend_of_Mana#cite_note-RETROseries-14)

_Legend of Mana_ was designed as a [2D](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2D_computer_graphics "2D computer graphics") game, despite the [PlayStation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_(console) "PlayStation (console)")'s [3D](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/3D_computer_graphics "3D computer graphics")-focus, as the console could not handle the full 3D world Ishii envisioned where one could interact with natural shaped objects.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legend_of_Mana#cite_note-loop-15) Kawazu initially let Ishii have a relaxed schedule and budget, as Ishii had a great number of ideas he wanted in the game, but when the project began to get out of control and out of time Kawazu tightened down the rest of the development schedule and convinced the Square executives to delay the game by two months—even though it had already been announced to the public—to allow it to be completed as Ishii envisioned. Content such as numerous character sprites and item [game mechanics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_mechanics "Game mechanics") had to be scrapped for the sake of fitting the whole game on one CD-ROM.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legend_of_Mana#cite_note-UltimaniaInt-16) Kawazu has said that this experience taught him that his true skill in game development lay in working as a producer.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legend_of_Mana#cite_note-VGMOBOXliner-17)

_Legend of Mana_ was first announced by Square in March 1999 just before its debut at the [Tokyo Game Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokyo_Game_Show "Tokyo Game Show").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legend_of_Mana#cite_note-announce-18) The game was released in Japan in July 1999 with considerable hype, packaged with demos of Square's future releases _[Vagrant Story](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vagrant\_Story "Vagrant Story")_, _[Chrono Cross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrono\_Cross "Chrono Cross")_, _[Front Mission 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Front\_Mission\_3 "Front Mission 3")_, and _[Threads of Fate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Threads\_of\_Fate "Threads of Fate")_.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legend_of_Mana#cite_note-hype-19) It was planned to be released in North America alongside the July and August 2000 releases of _Chrono Cross_ and _Threads of Fate_, but was instead released early on June 6.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legend_of_Mana#cite_note-GIrelease1-20)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legend_of_Mana#cite_note-GIrelease2-21)

The original score for _Legend of Mana_ was composed, arranged, and produced by Yoko Shimomura.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legend_of_Mana#cite_note-KikShimInt-22) Shimomura was a newcomer to the series; the previous two _Mana_ games were scored by [Hiroki Kikuta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hiroki_Kikuta "Hiroki Kikuta"), and the first by [Kenji Ito](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito "Kenji Ito").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legend_of_Mana#cite_note-SHint2-23) Shimomura said in 2002 that she considered the soundtrack to _Legend of Mana_ to be the one that best expresses herself.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legend_of_Mana#cite_note-SHIMOMURARBint-24) She claims that she prefers "passionate music that comes from the heart", and that she has to "feel the emotions of a piece in the extreme before I am able to write" the music by putting herself in the same mood as the piece is supposed to be in. _Legend of Mana_ featured the first vocal track of any _Mana_ game, "Song of Mana", which also serves as the game's opening theme. It was sung by [Swedish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sweden "Sweden") vocalist [Annika Ljungberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rednex#Permanent_members "Rednex"), who was chosen by Shimomura because she "wanted to stay away from working with someone popular that everyone already knows". After hearing a sample of Ljungberg's music, she flew to Sweden "straight away" to do an analog recording of the song.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legend_of_Mana#cite_note-KikShimInt-22)

The 1999 soundtrack album _Seiken Densetsu / Legend of Mana Original Soundtrack_ collects 55 tracks of music from _Legend of Mana_ on two discs. The music covers many styles including piano, hard rock, and electronic music. The soundtrack was published by [DigiCube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DigiCube "DigiCube"), and was reprinted by Square Enix in 2004.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legend_of_Mana#cite_note-RPGFLM-25) The album reached #65 on the Japanese [Oricon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oricon "Oricon") music charts and stayed on the charts for two weeks.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legend_of_Mana#cite_note-ORILOM-26) "Song of Mana" was later made available on the _[Square Vocal Collection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List\_of\_Square\_Enix\_compilation\_albums#Square\_Vocal\_Collection "List of Square Enix compilation albums")_ album in 2001.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legend_of_Mana#cite_note-RPGFLM-25) Four of the game's tracks were released as part of _[Drammatica: The Very Best Works of Yoko Shimomura](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List\_of\_Square\_Enix\_compilation\_albums#Drammatica "List of Square Enix compilation albums")_, an album of [arrangements](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrangement "Arrangement") highlighting the composer's work.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legend_of_Mana#cite_note-Drammatica's_Home_Page-27)

### Merchandise

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Legend_of_Mana&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Merchandise")]

Upon the game's Japanese release, several promotional items were made available from Square, including [stuffed toy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stuffed_toy "Stuffed toy") dolls of the rabite enemy and mascot of the series, a necklace, and lighters.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legend_of_Mana#cite_note-releasemerch-28)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legend_of_Mana#cite_note-EDGEretro-29) As a promotion for Square's "Summer of Adventure" release schedule in 2000, which the North American release of the game was a part of, those who preordered the game were given a free music CD with select tracks from the game.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legend_of_Mana#cite_note-preordermusic-30)_Legend of Mana_ was re-released in Japan late in 2000 as part of the Square Millennium Collection at a budget price along with a special [music box](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_box "Music box") and two character figurines.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legend_of_Mana#cite_note-SMC-31) A companion book titled _Seiken Densetsu: Legend of Mana Ultimania_ including artwork and interviews was released as part of Square's [_Ultimania_ series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Square_Enix_companion_books "List of Square Enix companion books"). It was published by [DigiCube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DigiCube "DigiCube") in 1999 and later reprinted by [Square Enix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Square_Enix "Square Enix") in 2004 after the subsidiary's closing.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legend_of_Mana#cite_note-BSlom-32) An artbook, _Legend of Mana: Making of Mana_, was published in 2000 by [ASCII](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ASCII_Corporation "ASCII Corporation").[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legend_of_Mana#cite_note-Making-33) A five-volume manga series, created by [Shiro Amano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shiro_Amano "Shiro Amano"), was published between 2000 and 2002.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legend_of_Mana#cite_note-manga-34)

In Japan, _Legend of Mana_ was a bestseller at the time of release,[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legend_of_Mana#cite_note-DENsales-43) and sold over 400,000 units in its first week alone as the highest-selling release that week in Japan.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legend_of_Mana#cite_note-400k-44) By the end of the year, it had sold over 700,000 copies in Japan.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legend_of_Mana#cite_note-TMB1999-45)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legend_of_Mana#cite_note-Gold-46)_Legend of Mana_ was also the top selling PlayStation game during the week of its release in North America.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legend_of_Mana#cite_note-NAsales-47)

_Legend of Mana_ received mixed reviews from critics.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legend_of_Mana#cite_note-GRankings-35) The game's presentation was almost universally praised, especially its use of vibrant and colorful hand-drawn graphics. David Smith of [IGN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IGN "IGN") claimed that the graphics were one of the game's best points, and RPGamer's Andrew P. Bilyk noted that the visuals "may be the most impressive two-dimensional graphics ever to grace an RPG".[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legend_of_Mana#cite_note-RPGamer-4)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legend_of_Mana#cite_note-IGNReview-40) Andrew Pfister of _[Electronic Gaming Monthly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic\_Gaming\_Monthly "Electronic Gaming Monthly")_ praised them even more, calling them "the most impressive 2D artwork ever seen on a console".[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legend_of_Mana#cite_note-EGMreview-48) Damian Thomas's RPGFan review likened the graphics to [Disney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Walt_Disney_Company "The Walt Disney Company") animation for having "a very storybook, cutesy cartoony feel to them", while Andrew Vestal of [GameSpot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GameSpot "GameSpot") said that the graphics were some of the most lush and ornate 2D graphics ever made.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legend_of_Mana#cite_note-GameSpotReview-5)[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legend_of_Mana#cite_note-RPGFan-49) The game won an award for best graphics at the 4th [Japan Game Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japan_Game_Awards "Japan Game Awards") from the [Computer Entertainment Supplier's Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_Entertainment_Supplier's_Association "Computer Entertainment Supplier's Association").[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legend_of_Mana#cite_note-Award-50) The music in _Legend of Mana_ was also a high point in many reviews; the reviewers for _Electronic Gaming Monthly_ called it "fantastic" and "wonderful".[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legend_of_Mana#cite_note-EGMreview-48) Smith of IGN's review stated that the soundtrack is "as good as any you'll hear today" with a good mix of intensity, suspense, and subtle nuance, and Vestal of GameSpot termed it "excellently orchestrated" and a perfect fit for the game in each environment.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legend_of_Mana#cite_note-GameSpotReview-5)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legend_of_Mana#cite_note-IGNReview-40)

Much of the game's criticism stemmed from its substitution of mostly unrelated quests over a main storyline. _[GamePro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GamePro "GamePro")_, while praising the Land Make system, found that the "focus of _Legend of Mana_ is obscured by the over-abundance of subplots".[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legend_of_Mana#cite_note-GamePro-6) Similarly, [Game Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_Revolution "Game Revolution")'s Johnny Liu commented that the game lacked depth and felt like a collection of short quests rather than a single game, while Vestal of GameSpot noted that the game's use of miniquests will likely disappoint those seeking an action-RPG classic, and said that, although fun, the gameplay had a "schizophrenic and disjointed nature".[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legend_of_Mana#cite_note-GameSpotReview-5)[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legend_of_Mana#cite_note-Revolution-51)_[Next Generation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Next\_Generation\_(magazine) "Next Generation (magazine)")_ agreed, saying that the Land Make system was an "innovative feature" but that it left the game disjointed without a solid plot to keep everything together.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legend_of_Mana#cite_note-NGreview-41) The Japanese _[Weekly Famitsu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Famitsu "Famitsu")_ reviewers felt that the system was ambitious, but left the game feeling disconnected, and that the divided plotlines kept the beginning of the game from having the charm of the end.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legend_of_Mana#cite_note-FAMreview-39)

Gary Steinman of _[Official U.S. PlayStation Magazine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Official\_U.S.\_PlayStation\_Magazine "Official U.S. PlayStation Magazine")_ said that the lack of a plotline gave the player no incentive to keep playing through what he felt was a poor combat system.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legend_of_Mana#cite_note-OPMreview-52) Both of those criticisms were repeated by _Electronic Gaming Monthly_'s Sam Kennedy in his review.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legend_of_Mana#cite_note-EGMreview-48) RPGamer's Bilyk felt that the smaller plots, while sometimes simplistic and not focused on the player, were enjoyable experiences.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legend_of_Mana#cite_note-RPGamer-4) IGN's Smith concluded that while he enjoyed the game, he felt that it was not a complete game like _Secret of Mana_, but instead a collection of fun experiences.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legend_of_Mana#cite_note-IGNReview-40)

**Koichi Ishii** (石井 浩一, _Ishii Kōichi_; born July 9, 1964[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koichi_Ishii#cite_note-profile-1)) is a Japanese [video game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Video_game "Video game") designer best known for creating the _[Mana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mana\_(series) "Mana (series)")_ series and founding [Grezzo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grezzo "Grezzo"). He joined [Square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Square_(video_game_company) "Square (video game company)") in 1986, where he has directed or produced every game released in the _Mana_ series (up to 2007). He has also contributed to several games in [Square Enix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Square_Enix "Square Enix")'s _[Final Fantasy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Final\_Fantasy "Final Fantasy")_ and _[SaGa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SaGa "SaGa")_ series, and created the well-known [chocobo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chocobo "Chocobo") and [moogle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moogle "Moogle") characters.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koichi_Ishii#cite_note-IGN-2)

## Biography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Koichi_Ishii&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Biography")]

### Square/Square Enix

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Koichi_Ishii&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Square/Square Enix")]

Koichi Ishii worked on the first three _Final Fantasy_ games, as well as _[SaGa Frontier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SaGa\_Frontier "SaGa Frontier")_.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koichi_Ishii#cite_note-IGN-2) He was invited to work on the original _Final Fantasy_ in 1986, and helped develop the crystal theme that became a recurring motif of the series.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koichi_Ishii#cite_note-up-3) Ishii became the head of Square Enix's Product Development Division 8.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koichi_Ishii#cite_note-fan-4)

### Mana series

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Koichi_Ishii&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Mana series")]

He wanted to create a game called _[Seiken Densetsu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seiken\_Densetsu "Seiken Densetsu")_ in 1987, but Square rejected the idea before he even finished planning it.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koichi_Ishii#cite_note-IGN-2) He was able to develop it in the early 1990s as a Final Fantasy [Gaiden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaiden "Gaiden").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koichi_Ishii#cite_note-IGN-2) He was involved in the development of the _[Sword of Mana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sword\_of\_Mana "Sword of Mana")_ and all other _[World of Mana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World\_of\_Mana "World of Mana")_ games.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koichi_Ishii#cite_note-IGN-2)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koichi_Ishii#cite_note-fan-4)

The _[World of Mana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World\_of\_Mana "World of Mana")_ series was conceived to be a way for players to experience the [_Mana_ series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mana_(series) "Mana (series)") in many formats and gameplay styles.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koichi_Ishii#cite_note-maana-5)

On _[Heroes of Mana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heroes\_of\_Mana "Heroes of Mana")_, development of a [real-time strategy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real-time_strategy "Real-time strategy") game became so difficult they had to start development all over at one point.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koichi_Ishii#cite_note-manass-6) Another challenge of game development was due to the Japanese gaming audiences lack of familiarity with an [RTS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real-time_strategy "Real-time strategy") style of gaming.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koichi_Ishii#cite_note-manass-6) The world of _[Seiken Densetsu 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seiken\_Densetsu\_3 "Seiken Densetsu 3")_ was chosen due to its plot involving warring states, which was thought to be well suited for an RTS game.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koichi_Ishii#cite_note-maana-5)

He left Square Enix after the release of the _World of Mana_ series. During the series' 30th anniversary livestream it was announced that a new entry in the franchise was in the early stages of development and that Ishii was involved with the project. The game titled _[Visions of Mana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visions\_of\_Mana "Visions of Mana")_ was released in August 2024.

### _Final Fantasy XI_

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Koichi_Ishii&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Final Fantasy XI")]

Ishii was also the original director for the [MMORPG](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MMORPG "MMORPG")_[Final Fantasy XI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Final\_Fantasy\_XI "Final Fantasy XI")_ and continued to be a central team member throughout the development of its first expansion, Rise of the Zilart.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koichi_Ishii#cite_note-Blue_Gartr-7) His guiding principle throughout the initial development cycle, according to a 2016 interview, was to both create compelling world and setting for the game as well as emphasize teamwork among players.

On the topic of creating the game's world, Vana'diel, he stated: "[FFXI is] a sandbox, I suppose. "There's the toy, let's dig holes and build castles," players would think. Creating an atmosphere where that will bring satisfaction was the goal." To support this design pattern, he claims to have deliberately spent time adding small atmospheric touches such as rainbows, hidden areas only reachable through exploration, auroras, flowers, and other "spontaneous events" that would draw the player into the game world. Ishii describes these as being quite important despite his perception of others viewing them as "pointless events."

In a [Famitsu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Famitsu "Famitsu") interview, he was quite vocal about using game mechanics to attempt to sculpt player behavior toward cooperation and teamwork. Ishii claims credit (alongside Hiroshi Takai, credited as an assistant director of _[Final Fantasy XIV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Final\_Fantasy\_XIV\_(2010\_video\_game) "Final Fantasy XIV (2010 video game)")_) for FFXI's skillchain system, by which players cooperate to time weapon skill abilities in concert to achieve bonus damage to an enemy monster. He explains that he created the system because he "thought it was important to create a sense of teamwork even while playing with strangers, and to that end [he] created the skillchain system." Two other areas he designed with teamwork in mind were the game economy and an EXP penalty upon death. The game economy was designed to make the player feel "insignificant" by emphasizing "production, consumption, and distribution," with the end goal of "understanding the importance of community." In a similar fashion, Ishii enforced an EXP penalty upon character death in FFXI because the player would "feel empathy for [his or her] teammates when they got knocked out."

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Koichi_Ishii&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Personal life")]

He joined game developer [Grezzo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grezzo "Grezzo") in April 2007.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koichi_Ishii#cite_note-profile-1) He has two sons, the first being born in April 1992.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koichi_Ishii#cite_note-8)

## Style and reception

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Koichi_Ishii&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Style and reception")]

_[IGN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IGN "IGN")_ named Ishii as one of the top 100 best game creators ever.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koichi_Ishii#cite_note-IGN-2) Ishii is noted for his use of an active real time battle system, a pioneering move at the time.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koichi_Ishii#cite_note-IGN-2) Some critics felt that the constant switching between a battle screen and the world map made the games feel faster paced and "deeper".[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koichi_Ishii#cite_note-IGN-2) He was also praised for his use of cutting-edge technologies such as [Mode 7](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mode_7 "Mode 7") graphics to create a 3D feel.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koichi_Ishii#cite_note-IGN-2)

**Koichi Ishii** (石井 浩一, _Ishii Kōichi_; born July 9, 1964[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koichi_Ishii#cite_note-profile-1)) is a Japanese [video game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Video_game "Video game") designer best known for creating the _[Mana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mana\_(series) "Mana (series)")_ series and founding [Grezzo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grezzo "Grezzo"). He joined [Square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Square_(video_game_company) "Square (video game company)") in 1986, where he has directed or produced every game released in the _Mana_ series (up to 2007). He has also contributed to several games in [Square Enix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Square_Enix "Square Enix")'s _[Final Fantasy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Final\_Fantasy "Final Fantasy")_ and _[SaGa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SaGa "SaGa")_ series, and created the well-known [chocobo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chocobo "Chocobo") and [moogle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moogle "Moogle") characters.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koichi_Ishii#cite_note-IGN-2)

## Biography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Koichi_Ishii&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Biography")]

### Square/Square Enix

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Koichi_Ishii&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Square/Square Enix")]

Koichi Ishii worked on the first three _Final Fantasy_ games, as well as _[SaGa Frontier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SaGa\_Frontier "SaGa Frontier")_.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koichi_Ishii#cite_note-IGN-2) He was invited to work on the original _Final Fantasy_ in 1986, and helped develop the crystal theme that became a recurring motif of the series.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koichi_Ishii#cite_note-up-3) Ishii became the head of Square Enix's Product Development Division 8.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koichi_Ishii#cite_note-fan-4)

### Mana series

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Koichi_Ishii&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Mana series")]

He wanted to create a game called _[Seiken Densetsu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seiken\_Densetsu "Seiken Densetsu")_ in 1987, but Square rejected the idea before he even finished planning it.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koichi_Ishii#cite_note-IGN-2) He was able to develop it in the early 1990s as a Final Fantasy [Gaiden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaiden "Gaiden").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koichi_Ishii#cite_note-IGN-2) He was involved in the development of the _[Sword of Mana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sword\_of\_Mana "Sword of Mana")_ and all other _[World of Mana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World\_of\_Mana "World of Mana")_ games.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koichi_Ishii#cite_note-IGN-2)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koichi_Ishii#cite_note-fan-4)

The _[World of Mana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World\_of\_Mana "World of Mana")_ series was conceived to be a way for players to experience the [_Mana_ series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mana_(series) "Mana (series)") in many formats and gameplay styles.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koichi_Ishii#cite_note-maana-5)

On _[Heroes of Mana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heroes\_of\_Mana "Heroes of Mana")_, development of a [real-time strategy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real-time_strategy "Real-time strategy") game became so difficult they had to start development all over at one point.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koichi_Ishii#cite_note-manass-6) Another challenge of game development was due to the Japanese gaming audiences lack of familiarity with an [RTS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real-time_strategy "Real-time strategy") style of gaming.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koichi_Ishii#cite_note-manass-6) The world of _[Seiken Densetsu 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seiken\_Densetsu\_3 "Seiken Densetsu 3")_ was chosen due to its plot involving warring states, which was thought to be well suited for an RTS game.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koichi_Ishii#cite_note-maana-5)

He left Square Enix after the release of the _World of Mana_ series. During the series' 30th anniversary livestream it was announced that a new entry in the franchise was in the early stages of development and that Ishii was involved with the project. The game titled _[Visions of Mana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visions\_of\_Mana "Visions of Mana")_ was released in August 2024.

### _Final Fantasy XI_

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Koichi_Ishii&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Final Fantasy XI")]

Ishii was also the original director for the [MMORPG](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MMORPG "MMORPG")_[Final Fantasy XI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Final\_Fantasy\_XI "Final Fantasy XI")_ and continued to be a central team member throughout the development of its first expansion, Rise of the Zilart.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koichi_Ishii#cite_note-Blue_Gartr-7) His guiding principle throughout the initial development cycle, according to a 2016 interview, was to both create compelling world and setting for the game as well as emphasize teamwork among players.

On the topic of creating the game's world, Vana'diel, he stated: "[FFXI is] a sandbox, I suppose. "There's the toy, let's dig holes and build castles," players would think. Creating an atmosphere where that will bring satisfaction was the goal." To support this design pattern, he claims to have deliberately spent time adding small atmospheric touches such as rainbows, hidden areas only reachable through exploration, auroras, flowers, and other "spontaneous events" that would draw the player into the game world. Ishii describes these as being quite important despite his perception of others viewing them as "pointless events."

In a [Famitsu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Famitsu "Famitsu") interview, he was quite vocal about using game mechanics to attempt to sculpt player behavior toward cooperation and teamwork. Ishii claims credit (alongside Hiroshi Takai, credited as an assistant director of _[Final Fantasy XIV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Final\_Fantasy\_XIV\_(2010\_video\_game) "Final Fantasy XIV (2010 video game)")_) for FFXI's skillchain system, by which players cooperate to time weapon skill abilities in concert to achieve bonus damage to an enemy monster. He explains that he created the system because he "thought it was important to create a sense of teamwork even while playing with strangers, and to that end [he] created the skillchain system." Two other areas he designed with teamwork in mind were the game economy and an EXP penalty upon death. The game economy was designed to make the player feel "insignificant" by emphasizing "production, consumption, and distribution," with the end goal of "understanding the importance of community." In a similar fashion, Ishii enforced an EXP penalty upon character death in FFXI because the player would "feel empathy for [his or her] teammates when they got knocked out."

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Koichi_Ishii&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Personal life")]

He joined game developer [Grezzo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grezzo "Grezzo") in April 2007.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koichi_Ishii#cite_note-profile-1) He has two sons, the first being born in April 1992.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koichi_Ishii#cite_note-8)

## Style and reception

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Koichi_Ishii&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Style and reception")]

_[IGN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IGN "IGN")_ named Ishii as one of the top 100 best game creators ever.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koichi_Ishii#cite_note-IGN-2) Ishii is noted for his use of an active real time battle system, a pioneering move at the time.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koichi_Ishii#cite_note-IGN-2) Some critics felt that the constant switching between a battle screen and the world map made the games feel faster paced and "deeper".[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koichi_Ishii#cite_note-IGN-2) He was also praised for his use of cutting-edge technologies such as [Mode 7](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mode_7 "Mode 7") graphics to create a 3D feel.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koichi_Ishii#cite_note-IGN-2)

**Kenji Ito** (伊藤 賢治, _\_Itō Kenji\__; born July 5, 1968), also known by the nickname **Itoken** (イトケン),[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-ITOsite-1)[[nb 1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-3) is a Japanese [video game composer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Video_game_music "Video game music") and musician. He is best known for his work on the _[Mana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mana\_(series) "Mana (series)")_ and _[SaGa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SaGa\_(series) "SaGa (series)")_ series, though he has worked on over 30 video games throughout his career as well as composed or arranged music for over 15 other albums, concerts, and plays. He learned to play several instruments at a young age, and joined [Square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Square_(video_game_company) "Square (video game company)") directly out of college as a composer in 1990 at the advice of a professor. He worked there for over a decade, composing many of his best-known scores. In 2001, he left Square to become a freelance composer, but has since continued to collaborate with the company.

Since leaving Square, Ito has composed soundtracks to over a dozen games, and has branched out into composition and production of music for plays and albums for other performers. Ito's work has been performed in a concert dedicated to his pieces as well as general video game music events, and he has played the piano in additional concerts. Pieces of his from the _SaGa_ and _Mana_ series have been arranged as piano solos and published in sheet music books.

## Biography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kenji_Ito&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Biography")]

### Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kenji_Ito&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Early life")]

Born in Tokyo, Japan, on July 5, 1968, Ito became interested in music at the age of four.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-ITOsite-1) He began to learn to play the piano, becoming interested in it after hearing piano music coming from a classroom he passed by daily with his mother. He was also interested in [Electone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electone "Electone") music, but was discouraged from learning it by a piano teacher.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-ITOCBint-4) By the time he began composing at the age of ten, he had learned to play alto saxophone, clarinet, and piano, and was interested in becoming a singer/songwriter.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-ITOsite-1) When he was close to graduating from college, he decided to pursue a career in composing music; when he asked a professor for advice, the professor recommended becoming a video game music composer, given the recent success in Japan of _[Dragon Quest III](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragon\_Quest\_III "Dragon Quest III")_. During March 1990, after applying to several video game companies including [HAL Laboratory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HAL_Laboratory "HAL Laboratory"), Ito began working at [Square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Square_(video_game_company) "Square (video game company)").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-Interview1-5)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-GAMAint-6)

### Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kenji_Ito&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Career")]

His first project was a co-effort that same year between himself and [Nobuo Uematsu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobuo_Uematsu "Nobuo Uematsu") for the [Game Boy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_Boy "Game Boy") title _[Final Fantasy Legend II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Final\_Fantasy\_Legend\_II "Final Fantasy Legend II")_ (_SaGa 2_).[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-ITOdisc-7) It led the following year to the first album release of his music, _[All Sounds of SaGa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music\_of\_the\_SaGa\_series "Music of the SaGa series")_, which was a combination album of _[The Final Fantasy Legend](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Final\_Fantasy\_Legend "The Final Fantasy Legend")_, _Final Fantasy Legend II_, and _[Final Fantasy Legend III](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Final\_Fantasy\_Legend\_III "Final Fantasy Legend III")_; all of Ito's work on _Legend II_ appeared on the album.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-RPGFASOS-8) Shortly after in 1991, he composed his first solo work, the soundtrack for _[Final Fantasy Adventure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Final\_Fantasy\_Adventure "Final Fantasy Adventure")_ (_Seiken Densetsu_), another Game Boy title. He then returned to the _SaGa_ series for the next few years, composing the soundtracks to the [Super Famicom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Famicom "Super Famicom")'s _[Romancing SaGa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romancing\_SaGa "Romancing SaGa")_, _[Romancing SaGa 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romancing\_SaGa\_2 "Romancing SaGa 2")_, and _[Romancing SaGa 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romancing\_SaGa\_3 "Romancing SaGa 3")_.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-ITOdisc-7) These soundtracks sparked Ito's first arranged albums; the first game was arranged in a French musical style by Masaaki Mizuguchi, while the other two were arranged by Ryou Fukui and Taro Iwashiro, respectively, into orchestral pieces.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-RPGFRSLR-9)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-RPGFRS2ER-10)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-RPGFRS3WT-11) Ito was originally scheduled to continue on with the [_Mana_ series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mana_(series) "Mana (series)") and compose the soundtrack to _Seiken Densetsu 2_ (_[Secret of Mana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret\_of\_Mana "Secret of Mana")_), but was forced to hand the project off to [Hiroki Kikuta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hiroki_Kikuta "Hiroki Kikuta") as his first score due to the demand on his time for scoring _Romancing SaGa_.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-SHint2-12)

1995 marked the first time since he started composing that he worked on a title outside the _Mana_ or [_SaGa_ series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SaGa_(series) "SaGa (series)"); he composed the music for _Koi wa Balance_ and was a member of an eight-person team for _[Tobal No. 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tobal\_No.\_1 "Tobal No. 1")_. He returned to the _SaGa_ series in 1997 with _[SaGa Frontier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SaGa\_Frontier "SaGa Frontier")_, and finished out the decade with _[Chocobo Racing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chocobo\_Racing "Chocobo Racing")_ and _[Chocobo's Dungeon 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chocobo's\_Dungeon\_2 "Chocobo's Dungeon 2")_; for _Chocobo Racing_ he only arranged previous works from the _[Chocobo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chocobo\_(series) "Chocobo (series)")_ and _Final Fantasy_ series, and contributed only a few tracks to _Chocobo's Dungeon 2_.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-ITOdisc-7) He left Square in 2001 to become a freelance composer. He has said that this move was in order to give him the flexibility to work on more than just video game music.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-Interview1-5)

The first work that Ito composed after leaving Square was the soundtrack to _[Culdcept II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Culdcept\_II "Culdcept II")_, which he regards as his best work. He attributes this feeling both to the fact that it was his first freelance piece and that he handled all aspects of the music production, from composition through arrangement and sound production.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-ITOCBint-4) From there he returned to working with Square and the _Mana_ series with the remake of his second soundtrack, _Final Fantasy Adventure_, into the soundtrack of _[Sword of Mana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sword\_of\_Mana "Sword of Mana")_. It was an act he would repeat two years later for Square, now [Square Enix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Square_Enix "Square Enix"), with the remake of _Romancing SaGa_, _Romancing SaGa: Minstrel Song_. He has since returned to the _Mana_ series twice, with the soundtracks to _[Children of Mana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Children\_of\_Mana "Children of Mana")_ and _[Dawn of Mana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dawn\_of\_Mana "Dawn of Mana")_. All of the video game soundtracks that he has composed since the third expansion pack for _[Cross Gate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cross\_Gate "Cross Gate")_ in 2004 have been with the assistance of other composers except for 2007's _[Hero Must Die](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hero\_Must\_Die "Hero Must Die")_, though during those years he has branched out from video games into composing and producing albums and singles for performers as well as composing music for plays and concerts.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-ITOdisc-7) He has also released an album of piano pieces that he has composed; only two of the eight tracks are from his video game works.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-Japdisc-13)

## Legacy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kenji_Ito&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Legacy")]

Ito performed piano live during September 22, 2006 _Press Start 2006 -Symphony of Games-_ live concert, at which several of his pieces were performed by an orchestra.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-GAMAint-6) This concert followed a concert of August 26, 2006 _Manami Kiyota x Kenji Ito Collaboration Live_ in which he played the piano for songs composed by him for the event and sung by Manami Kiyota; he has also played the piano at concerts given by _[The Black Mages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Black\_Mages "The Black Mages")_, a band composed of current or former Square musicians, before they expanded to include a full-time pianist.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-COCOEnews-14) Music composed by Ito has also been performed at the _Extra -Hyper Game Music Event 2007_ and _Christmas Live 2008 "gentleecho -prelude-"_ concerts.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-Japdisc-13)

Music composed by Ito was performed at a concert devoted to his music on February 21, 2009 titled "gentle echo meeting" at the Uchisaiwaicho Hall in Chiyoda, Tokyo. A group of five musicians performed eight of his songs, interspersed with performances by Ito and discussions about his music between himself and [Masahiro Sakurai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Masahiro_Sakurai "Masahiro Sakurai"). The event began as a concert due to Ito's wish to host one based on his music, but after the space the organizing company, Harmonics International, rented turned out to be run by a high school classmate of Ito, at the classmate's insistence the discussions of Ito's music were added to the program.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-GAMAint-6)

Music from the original soundtracks of _Dawn of Mana_ and _Sword of Mana_ has been arranged for the piano and published by DOREMI Music Publishing.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-DOREMI-15) Two compilation books of music from the series as a whole have also been published as _Seiken Densetsu Best Collection Piano Solo Sheet Music_ first and second editions, with the first edition including tracks by Ito from _Final Fantasy Adventure_ while the second added tracks he composed from _Dawn of Mana_. All songs in each book have been rewritten by Asako Niwa as beginning to intermediate level piano solos, though they are meant to sound as much like the originals as possible.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-SEMOsheet-16) Additionally, KMP Music Publishing has published a book of the piano music included in the _Sword of Mana_ soundtrack album, which Ito arranged from his original compositions.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-SEMOSOMsheet-17) DOREMI Music Publishing also published music from the original soundtracks of some of the _SaGa_ games that Ito composed as piano sheet music book; music from _Romancing SaGa 3_, _Romancing SaGa Minstrel Song_, and _SaGa Frontier_ were written by Asako Niwa for piano solos of beginning to intermediate difficulty.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-DOREMI-15)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-SEMOsheetS-18)

## Musical style and influences

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kenji_Ito&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Musical style and influences")]

Ito's music is mainly inspired by images from the game rather than outside influences; however, he never played the games themselves. The only video games that he plays are [sports games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sports_game "Sports game"); he has only seen up to the introductory movie for most of the role-playing games that he has written music for.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-ITOCBint-4)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-Interview1-5) While many of his pieces are orchestral, he enjoys working in a recording studio and enjoys composing "normal songs" as much as his orchestral works.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-Interview1-5) His favorite video game music from other composers include the music from _[Star Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star\_Fox\_(series) "Star Fox (series)")_, _[Dragon Quest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragon\_Quest "Dragon Quest")_, _[Final Fantasy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Final\_Fantasy "Final Fantasy")_, _[Wizardry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wizardry\_(video\_game\_series) "Wizardry (video game series)")_ and _[Nobunaga's Ambition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobunaga's\_Ambition "Nobunaga's Ambition")_. Non-video game music that has inspired him includes Japanese popular music and soundtracks to [anime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anime "Anime") works, as well as easy listening music such as [Paul Mauriat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Mauriat "Paul Mauriat") or [Richard Clayderman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Clayderman "Richard Clayderman"), especially [string music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/String_instrument "String instrument").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-Interview1-5) These influences have led him to wish to create music "that you can listen to while you relax". He also wishes to expand his compositions outside video game music and into ballads.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-GAMAint-6)

**Kenji Ito** (伊藤 賢治, _\_Itō Kenji\__; born July 5, 1968), also known by the nickname **Itoken** (イトケン),[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-ITOsite-1)[[nb 1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-3) is a Japanese [video game composer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Video_game_music "Video game music") and musician. He is best known for his work on the _[Mana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mana\_(series) "Mana (series)")_ and _[SaGa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SaGa\_(series) "SaGa (series)")_ series, though he has worked on over 30 video games throughout his career as well as composed or arranged music for over 15 other albums, concerts, and plays. He learned to play several instruments at a young age, and joined [Square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Square_(video_game_company) "Square (video game company)") directly out of college as a composer in 1990 at the advice of a professor. He worked there for over a decade, composing many of his best-known scores. In 2001, he left Square to become a freelance composer, but has since continued to collaborate with the company.

Since leaving Square, Ito has composed soundtracks to over a dozen games, and has branched out into composition and production of music for plays and albums for other performers. Ito's work has been performed in a concert dedicated to his pieces as well as general video game music events, and he has played the piano in additional concerts. Pieces of his from the _SaGa_ and _Mana_ series have been arranged as piano solos and published in sheet music books.

## Biography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kenji_Ito&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Biography")]

### Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kenji_Ito&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Early life")]

Born in Tokyo, Japan, on July 5, 1968, Ito became interested in music at the age of four.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-ITOsite-1) He began to learn to play the piano, becoming interested in it after hearing piano music coming from a classroom he passed by daily with his mother. He was also interested in [Electone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electone "Electone") music, but was discouraged from learning it by a piano teacher.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-ITOCBint-4) By the time he began composing at the age of ten, he had learned to play alto saxophone, clarinet, and piano, and was interested in becoming a singer/songwriter.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-ITOsite-1) When he was close to graduating from college, he decided to pursue a career in composing music; when he asked a professor for advice, the professor recommended becoming a video game music composer, given the recent success in Japan of _[Dragon Quest III](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragon\_Quest\_III "Dragon Quest III")_. During March 1990, after applying to several video game companies including [HAL Laboratory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HAL_Laboratory "HAL Laboratory"), Ito began working at [Square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Square_(video_game_company) "Square (video game company)").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-Interview1-5)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-GAMAint-6)

### Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kenji_Ito&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Career")]

His first project was a co-effort that same year between himself and [Nobuo Uematsu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobuo_Uematsu "Nobuo Uematsu") for the [Game Boy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_Boy "Game Boy") title _[Final Fantasy Legend II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Final\_Fantasy\_Legend\_II "Final Fantasy Legend II")_ (_SaGa 2_).[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-ITOdisc-7) It led the following year to the first album release of his music, _[All Sounds of SaGa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music\_of\_the\_SaGa\_series "Music of the SaGa series")_, which was a combination album of _[The Final Fantasy Legend](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Final\_Fantasy\_Legend "The Final Fantasy Legend")_, _Final Fantasy Legend II_, and _[Final Fantasy Legend III](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Final\_Fantasy\_Legend\_III "Final Fantasy Legend III")_; all of Ito's work on _Legend II_ appeared on the album.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-RPGFASOS-8) Shortly after in 1991, he composed his first solo work, the soundtrack for _[Final Fantasy Adventure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Final\_Fantasy\_Adventure "Final Fantasy Adventure")_ (_Seiken Densetsu_), another Game Boy title. He then returned to the _SaGa_ series for the next few years, composing the soundtracks to the [Super Famicom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Famicom "Super Famicom")'s _[Romancing SaGa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romancing\_SaGa "Romancing SaGa")_, _[Romancing SaGa 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romancing\_SaGa\_2 "Romancing SaGa 2")_, and _[Romancing SaGa 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romancing\_SaGa\_3 "Romancing SaGa 3")_.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-ITOdisc-7) These soundtracks sparked Ito's first arranged albums; the first game was arranged in a French musical style by Masaaki Mizuguchi, while the other two were arranged by Ryou Fukui and Taro Iwashiro, respectively, into orchestral pieces.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-RPGFRSLR-9)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-RPGFRS2ER-10)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-RPGFRS3WT-11) Ito was originally scheduled to continue on with the [_Mana_ series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mana_(series) "Mana (series)") and compose the soundtrack to _Seiken Densetsu 2_ (_[Secret of Mana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret\_of\_Mana "Secret of Mana")_), but was forced to hand the project off to [Hiroki Kikuta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hiroki_Kikuta "Hiroki Kikuta") as his first score due to the demand on his time for scoring _Romancing SaGa_.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-SHint2-12)

1995 marked the first time since he started composing that he worked on a title outside the _Mana_ or [_SaGa_ series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SaGa_(series) "SaGa (series)"); he composed the music for _Koi wa Balance_ and was a member of an eight-person team for _[Tobal No. 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tobal\_No.\_1 "Tobal No. 1")_. He returned to the _SaGa_ series in 1997 with _[SaGa Frontier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SaGa\_Frontier "SaGa Frontier")_, and finished out the decade with _[Chocobo Racing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chocobo\_Racing "Chocobo Racing")_ and _[Chocobo's Dungeon 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chocobo's\_Dungeon\_2 "Chocobo's Dungeon 2")_; for _Chocobo Racing_ he only arranged previous works from the _[Chocobo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chocobo\_(series) "Chocobo (series)")_ and _Final Fantasy_ series, and contributed only a few tracks to _Chocobo's Dungeon 2_.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-ITOdisc-7) He left Square in 2001 to become a freelance composer. He has said that this move was in order to give him the flexibility to work on more than just video game music.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-Interview1-5)

The first work that Ito composed after leaving Square was the soundtrack to _[Culdcept II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Culdcept\_II "Culdcept II")_, which he regards as his best work. He attributes this feeling both to the fact that it was his first freelance piece and that he handled all aspects of the music production, from composition through arrangement and sound production.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-ITOCBint-4) From there he returned to working with Square and the _Mana_ series with the remake of his second soundtrack, _Final Fantasy Adventure_, into the soundtrack of _[Sword of Mana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sword\_of\_Mana "Sword of Mana")_. It was an act he would repeat two years later for Square, now [Square Enix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Square_Enix "Square Enix"), with the remake of _Romancing SaGa_, _Romancing SaGa: Minstrel Song_. He has since returned to the _Mana_ series twice, with the soundtracks to _[Children of Mana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Children\_of\_Mana "Children of Mana")_ and _[Dawn of Mana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dawn\_of\_Mana "Dawn of Mana")_. All of the video game soundtracks that he has composed since the third expansion pack for _[Cross Gate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cross\_Gate "Cross Gate")_ in 2004 have been with the assistance of other composers except for 2007's _[Hero Must Die](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hero\_Must\_Die "Hero Must Die")_, though during those years he has branched out from video games into composing and producing albums and singles for performers as well as composing music for plays and concerts.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-ITOdisc-7) He has also released an album of piano pieces that he has composed; only two of the eight tracks are from his video game works.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-Japdisc-13)

## Legacy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kenji_Ito&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Legacy")]

Ito performed piano live during September 22, 2006 _Press Start 2006 -Symphony of Games-_ live concert, at which several of his pieces were performed by an orchestra.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-GAMAint-6) This concert followed a concert of August 26, 2006 _Manami Kiyota x Kenji Ito Collaboration Live_ in which he played the piano for songs composed by him for the event and sung by Manami Kiyota; he has also played the piano at concerts given by _[The Black Mages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Black\_Mages "The Black Mages")_, a band composed of current or former Square musicians, before they expanded to include a full-time pianist.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-COCOEnews-14) Music composed by Ito has also been performed at the _Extra -Hyper Game Music Event 2007_ and _Christmas Live 2008 "gentleecho -prelude-"_ concerts.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-Japdisc-13)

Music composed by Ito was performed at a concert devoted to his music on February 21, 2009 titled "gentle echo meeting" at the Uchisaiwaicho Hall in Chiyoda, Tokyo. A group of five musicians performed eight of his songs, interspersed with performances by Ito and discussions about his music between himself and [Masahiro Sakurai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Masahiro_Sakurai "Masahiro Sakurai"). The event began as a concert due to Ito's wish to host one based on his music, but after the space the organizing company, Harmonics International, rented turned out to be run by a high school classmate of Ito, at the classmate's insistence the discussions of Ito's music were added to the program.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-GAMAint-6)

Music from the original soundtracks of _Dawn of Mana_ and _Sword of Mana_ has been arranged for the piano and published by DOREMI Music Publishing.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-DOREMI-15) Two compilation books of music from the series as a whole have also been published as _Seiken Densetsu Best Collection Piano Solo Sheet Music_ first and second editions, with the first edition including tracks by Ito from _Final Fantasy Adventure_ while the second added tracks he composed from _Dawn of Mana_. All songs in each book have been rewritten by Asako Niwa as beginning to intermediate level piano solos, though they are meant to sound as much like the originals as possible.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-SEMOsheet-16) Additionally, KMP Music Publishing has published a book of the piano music included in the _Sword of Mana_ soundtrack album, which Ito arranged from his original compositions.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-SEMOSOMsheet-17) DOREMI Music Publishing also published music from the original soundtracks of some of the _SaGa_ games that Ito composed as piano sheet music book; music from _Romancing SaGa 3_, _Romancing SaGa Minstrel Song_, and _SaGa Frontier_ were written by Asako Niwa for piano solos of beginning to intermediate difficulty.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-DOREMI-15)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-SEMOsheetS-18)

## Musical style and influences

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kenji_Ito&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Musical style and influences")]

Ito's music is mainly inspired by images from the game rather than outside influences; however, he never played the games themselves. The only video games that he plays are [sports games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sports_game "Sports game"); he has only seen up to the introductory movie for most of the role-playing games that he has written music for.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-ITOCBint-4)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-Interview1-5) While many of his pieces are orchestral, he enjoys working in a recording studio and enjoys composing "normal songs" as much as his orchestral works.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-Interview1-5) His favorite video game music from other composers include the music from _[Star Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star\_Fox\_(series) "Star Fox (series)")_, _[Dragon Quest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragon\_Quest "Dragon Quest")_, _[Final Fantasy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Final\_Fantasy "Final Fantasy")_, _[Wizardry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wizardry\_(video\_game\_series) "Wizardry (video game series)")_ and _[Nobunaga's Ambition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobunaga's\_Ambition "Nobunaga's Ambition")_. Non-video game music that has inspired him includes Japanese popular music and soundtracks to [anime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anime "Anime") works, as well as easy listening music such as [Paul Mauriat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Mauriat "Paul Mauriat") or [Richard Clayderman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Clayderman "Richard Clayderman"), especially [string music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/String_instrument "String instrument").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-Interview1-5) These influences have led him to wish to create music "that you can listen to while you relax". He also wishes to expand his compositions outside video game music and into ballads.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-GAMAint-6)
