**Kenji Ito** (伊藤 賢治, _\_Itō Kenji\__; born July 5, 1968), also known by the nickname **Itoken** (イトケン),[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-ITOsite-1)[[nb 1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-3) is a Japanese [video game composer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Video_game_music "Video game music") and musician. He is best known for his work on the _[Mana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mana\_(series) "Mana (series)")_ and _[SaGa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SaGa\_(series) "SaGa (series)")_ series, though he has worked on over 30 video games throughout his career as well as composed or arranged music for over 15 other albums, concerts, and plays. He learned to play several instruments at a young age, and joined [Square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Square_(video_game_company) "Square (video game company)") directly out of college as a composer in 1990 at the advice of a professor. He worked there for over a decade, composing many of his best-known scores. In 2001, he left Square to become a freelance composer, but has since continued to collaborate with the company.

Since leaving Square, Ito has composed soundtracks to over a dozen games, and has branched out into composition and production of music for plays and albums for other performers. Ito's work has been performed in a concert dedicated to his pieces as well as general video game music events, and he has played the piano in additional concerts. Pieces of his from the _SaGa_ and _Mana_ series have been arranged as piano solos and published in sheet music books.

## Biography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kenji_Ito&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Biography")]

### Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kenji_Ito&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Early life")]

Born in Tokyo, Japan, on July 5, 1968, Ito became interested in music at the age of four.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-ITOsite-1) He began to learn to play the piano, becoming interested in it after hearing piano music coming from a classroom he passed by daily with his mother. He was also interested in [Electone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electone "Electone") music, but was discouraged from learning it by a piano teacher.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-ITOCBint-4) By the time he began composing at the age of ten, he had learned to play alto saxophone, clarinet, and piano, and was interested in becoming a singer/songwriter.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-ITOsite-1) When he was close to graduating from college, he decided to pursue a career in composing music; when he asked a professor for advice, the professor recommended becoming a video game music composer, given the recent success in Japan of _[Dragon Quest III](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragon\_Quest\_III "Dragon Quest III")_. During March 1990, after applying to several video game companies including [HAL Laboratory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HAL_Laboratory "HAL Laboratory"), Ito began working at [Square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Square_(video_game_company) "Square (video game company)").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-Interview1-5)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-GAMAint-6)

### Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kenji_Ito&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Career")]

His first project was a co-effort that same year between himself and [Nobuo Uematsu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobuo_Uematsu "Nobuo Uematsu") for the [Game Boy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_Boy "Game Boy") title _[Final Fantasy Legend II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Final\_Fantasy\_Legend\_II "Final Fantasy Legend II")_ (_SaGa 2_).[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-ITOdisc-7) It led the following year to the first album release of his music, _[All Sounds of SaGa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music\_of\_the\_SaGa\_series "Music of the SaGa series")_, which was a combination album of _[The Final Fantasy Legend](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Final\_Fantasy\_Legend "The Final Fantasy Legend")_, _Final Fantasy Legend II_, and _[Final Fantasy Legend III](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Final\_Fantasy\_Legend\_III "Final Fantasy Legend III")_; all of Ito's work on _Legend II_ appeared on the album.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-RPGFASOS-8) Shortly after in 1991, he composed his first solo work, the soundtrack for _[Final Fantasy Adventure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Final\_Fantasy\_Adventure "Final Fantasy Adventure")_ (_Seiken Densetsu_), another Game Boy title. He then returned to the _SaGa_ series for the next few years, composing the soundtracks to the [Super Famicom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Famicom "Super Famicom")'s _[Romancing SaGa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romancing\_SaGa "Romancing SaGa")_, _[Romancing SaGa 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romancing\_SaGa\_2 "Romancing SaGa 2")_, and _[Romancing SaGa 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romancing\_SaGa\_3 "Romancing SaGa 3")_.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-ITOdisc-7) These soundtracks sparked Ito's first arranged albums; the first game was arranged in a French musical style by Masaaki Mizuguchi, while the other two were arranged by Ryou Fukui and Taro Iwashiro, respectively, into orchestral pieces.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-RPGFRSLR-9)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-RPGFRS2ER-10)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-RPGFRS3WT-11) Ito was originally scheduled to continue on with the [_Mana_ series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mana_(series) "Mana (series)") and compose the soundtrack to _Seiken Densetsu 2_ (_[Secret of Mana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret\_of\_Mana "Secret of Mana")_), but was forced to hand the project off to [Hiroki Kikuta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hiroki_Kikuta "Hiroki Kikuta") as his first score due to the demand on his time for scoring _Romancing SaGa_.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-SHint2-12)

1995 marked the first time since he started composing that he worked on a title outside the _Mana_ or [_SaGa_ series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SaGa_(series) "SaGa (series)"); he composed the music for _Koi wa Balance_ and was a member of an eight-person team for _[Tobal No. 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tobal\_No.\_1 "Tobal No. 1")_. He returned to the _SaGa_ series in 1997 with _[SaGa Frontier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SaGa\_Frontier "SaGa Frontier")_, and finished out the decade with _[Chocobo Racing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chocobo\_Racing "Chocobo Racing")_ and _[Chocobo's Dungeon 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chocobo's\_Dungeon\_2 "Chocobo's Dungeon 2")_; for _Chocobo Racing_ he only arranged previous works from the _[Chocobo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chocobo\_(series) "Chocobo (series)")_ and _Final Fantasy_ series, and contributed only a few tracks to _Chocobo's Dungeon 2_.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-ITOdisc-7) He left Square in 2001 to become a freelance composer. He has said that this move was in order to give him the flexibility to work on more than just video game music.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-Interview1-5)

The first work that Ito composed after leaving Square was the soundtrack to _[Culdcept II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Culdcept\_II "Culdcept II")_, which he regards as his best work. He attributes this feeling both to the fact that it was his first freelance piece and that he handled all aspects of the music production, from composition through arrangement and sound production.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-ITOCBint-4) From there he returned to working with Square and the _Mana_ series with the remake of his second soundtrack, _Final Fantasy Adventure_, into the soundtrack of _[Sword of Mana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sword\_of\_Mana "Sword of Mana")_. It was an act he would repeat two years later for Square, now [Square Enix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Square_Enix "Square Enix"), with the remake of _Romancing SaGa_, _Romancing SaGa: Minstrel Song_. He has since returned to the _Mana_ series twice, with the soundtracks to _[Children of Mana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Children\_of\_Mana "Children of Mana")_ and _[Dawn of Mana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dawn\_of\_Mana "Dawn of Mana")_. All of the video game soundtracks that he has composed since the third expansion pack for _[Cross Gate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cross\_Gate "Cross Gate")_ in 2004 have been with the assistance of other composers except for 2007's _[Hero Must Die](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hero\_Must\_Die "Hero Must Die")_, though during those years he has branched out from video games into composing and producing albums and singles for performers as well as composing music for plays and concerts.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-ITOdisc-7) He has also released an album of piano pieces that he has composed; only two of the eight tracks are from his video game works.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-Japdisc-13)

## Legacy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kenji_Ito&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Legacy")]

Ito performed piano live during September 22, 2006 _Press Start 2006 -Symphony of Games-_ live concert, at which several of his pieces were performed by an orchestra.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-GAMAint-6) This concert followed a concert of August 26, 2006 _Manami Kiyota x Kenji Ito Collaboration Live_ in which he played the piano for songs composed by him for the event and sung by Manami Kiyota; he has also played the piano at concerts given by _[The Black Mages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Black\_Mages "The Black Mages")_, a band composed of current or former Square musicians, before they expanded to include a full-time pianist.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-COCOEnews-14) Music composed by Ito has also been performed at the _Extra -Hyper Game Music Event 2007_ and _Christmas Live 2008 "gentleecho -prelude-"_ concerts.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-Japdisc-13)

Music composed by Ito was performed at a concert devoted to his music on February 21, 2009 titled "gentle echo meeting" at the Uchisaiwaicho Hall in Chiyoda, Tokyo. A group of five musicians performed eight of his songs, interspersed with performances by Ito and discussions about his music between himself and [Masahiro Sakurai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Masahiro_Sakurai "Masahiro Sakurai"). The event began as a concert due to Ito's wish to host one based on his music, but after the space the organizing company, Harmonics International, rented turned out to be run by a high school classmate of Ito, at the classmate's insistence the discussions of Ito's music were added to the program.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-GAMAint-6)

Music from the original soundtracks of _Dawn of Mana_ and _Sword of Mana_ has been arranged for the piano and published by DOREMI Music Publishing.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-DOREMI-15) Two compilation books of music from the series as a whole have also been published as _Seiken Densetsu Best Collection Piano Solo Sheet Music_ first and second editions, with the first edition including tracks by Ito from _Final Fantasy Adventure_ while the second added tracks he composed from _Dawn of Mana_. All songs in each book have been rewritten by Asako Niwa as beginning to intermediate level piano solos, though they are meant to sound as much like the originals as possible.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-SEMOsheet-16) Additionally, KMP Music Publishing has published a book of the piano music included in the _Sword of Mana_ soundtrack album, which Ito arranged from his original compositions.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-SEMOSOMsheet-17) DOREMI Music Publishing also published music from the original soundtracks of some of the _SaGa_ games that Ito composed as piano sheet music book; music from _Romancing SaGa 3_, _Romancing SaGa Minstrel Song_, and _SaGa Frontier_ were written by Asako Niwa for piano solos of beginning to intermediate difficulty.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-DOREMI-15)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-SEMOsheetS-18)

## Musical style and influences

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kenji_Ito&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Musical style and influences")]

Ito's music is mainly inspired by images from the game rather than outside influences; however, he never played the games themselves. The only video games that he plays are [sports games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sports_game "Sports game"); he has only seen up to the introductory movie for most of the role-playing games that he has written music for.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-ITOCBint-4)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-Interview1-5) While many of his pieces are orchestral, he enjoys working in a recording studio and enjoys composing "normal songs" as much as his orchestral works.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-Interview1-5) His favorite video game music from other composers include the music from _[Star Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star\_Fox\_(series) "Star Fox (series)")_, _[Dragon Quest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragon\_Quest "Dragon Quest")_, _[Final Fantasy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Final\_Fantasy "Final Fantasy")_, _[Wizardry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wizardry\_(video\_game\_series) "Wizardry (video game series)")_ and _[Nobunaga's Ambition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobunaga's\_Ambition "Nobunaga's Ambition")_. Non-video game music that has inspired him includes Japanese popular music and soundtracks to [anime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anime "Anime") works, as well as easy listening music such as [Paul Mauriat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Mauriat "Paul Mauriat") or [Richard Clayderman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Clayderman "Richard Clayderman"), especially [string music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/String_instrument "String instrument").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-Interview1-5) These influences have led him to wish to create music "that you can listen to while you relax". He also wishes to expand his compositions outside video game music and into ballads.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito#cite_note-GAMAint-6)

_**Secret of Mana**_, originally released in Japan as _**Seiken Densetsu 2**_,[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-1) is a 1993 [action role-playing game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Action_role-playing_game "Action role-playing game") developed and published by [Square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Square_(video_game_company) "Square (video game company)") for the [Super Nintendo Entertainment System](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Nintendo_Entertainment_System "Super Nintendo Entertainment System"). It is the sequel to the 1991 game _[Seiken Densetsu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Final\_Fantasy\_Adventure "Final Fantasy Adventure")_, released in North America as _Final Fantasy Adventure_ and in Europe as _Mystic Quest_. _Secret of Mana_ was the first _Seiken Densetsu_ title to be marketed as part of the [_Mana_ series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mana_(series) "Mana (series)") rather than the _[Final Fantasy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Final\_Fantasy "Final Fantasy")_ series. Set in a [high fantasy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High_fantasy "High fantasy") universe, the game follows three heroes as they attempt to prevent an empire from conquering the world with the power of an ancient flying fortress.

Rather than using a [turn-based](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turn-based "Turn-based") battle system like contemporaneous role-playing games, _Secret of Mana_ features [real-time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real-time_game "Real-time game") battles with a power bar mechanic. The game has a unique [Ring Command](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pie_menu "Pie menu") menu system, which [pauses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pausable_real-time "Pausable real-time") the action and allows the player to make decisions in the middle of battle. An innovative [cooperative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cooperative_video_game "Cooperative video game")[multiplayer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multiplayer_video_game "Multiplayer video game") system allows a second or third player to drop in and out of the game at any time. _Secret of Mana_ was directed and designed by Koichi Ishii, programmed primarily by [Nasir Gebelli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nasir_Gebelli "Nasir Gebelli"), and produced by veteran Square designer [Hiromichi Tanaka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hiromichi_Tanaka "Hiromichi Tanaka").

The game received acclaim for its brightly colored graphics, expansive plot, Ring Command menu system, and innovative real-time battle system. Critics also praised [Hiroki Kikuta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hiroki_Kikuta "Hiroki Kikuta")'s soundtrack and the customizable [artificial intelligence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_intelligence_(video_games) "Artificial intelligence (video games)") settings for computer-controlled allies. Retrospectively, it has been considered one of the [greatest games of all time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_video_games_listed_among_the_best "List of video games listed among the best") by critics. It was re-released on Virtual Console on the [Wii](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wii "Wii") in 2008 and [Wii U](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wii_U "Wii U") in 2013, as an enhanced version on multiple mobile platforms between 2009 and 2019, on [Switch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nintendo_Switch "Nintendo Switch") as part of _[Collection of Mana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Collection\_of\_Mana "Collection of Mana")_ in 2017 and 2019, and was remade in 3D in 2018 for [PlayStation 4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_4 "PlayStation 4"), [Vita](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Vita "PlayStation Vita") and [Windows](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windows "Windows"). The remake saw mixed reviews, with many faulting its lack of gameplay improvements and reworked graphics.

## Gameplay

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Secret_of_Mana&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Gameplay")]

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/f/f0/Smana.PNG/250px-Smana.PNG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Smana.PNG)

The standard overhead view. The party's attack strength and remaining [health](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Health_(gaming) "Health (gaming)") is shown in the gauges at the bottom.

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/5/5c/Flammie_Flying.gif/250px-Flammie_Flying.gif?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Flammie_Flying.gif)

Flammie flying and demonstrating [Mode 7](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mode_7 "Mode 7")

Like many other role-playing games of the [16-bit era](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_video_game_consoles_(fourth_generation) "History of video game consoles (fourth generation)"), _Secret of Mana_ displays a [top-down perspective](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Top-down_perspective "Top-down perspective"), in which the [player characters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Player_characters "Player characters") navigate the terrain and fight off hostile creatures. The game features three such characters: the hero, the girl, and the [sprite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sprite_(folklore) "Sprite (folklore)"), named Randi, Primm, and Popoi outside the initial North American and European releases. The player can also choose their own names for them. The player can choose to control each of the characters at any time; whichever character is currently selected, the other two companions are controlled via [artificial intelligence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_intelligence_(video_games) "Artificial intelligence (video games)"). The game may be played simultaneously by up to three players,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-RPGFan-2)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-RPGamer-3) made possible by the [Super Multitap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Multitap "Super Multitap") accessory for the [Super NES](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Nintendo_Entertainment_System "Super Nintendo Entertainment System") console.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-NPower_1-4) The [Virtual Console](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virtual_Console "Virtual Console") version of the game supports three-player gameplay via additional [GameCube controllers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nintendo_GameCube_controller "Nintendo GameCube controller") or [Classic Controllers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Classic_Controller "Classic Controller").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-vc_ign-5)

Each character possesses individual strengths and weaknesses. The hero, while unable to use magic, masters weapons at a quicker rate; the girl is a [healer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Healer_(gaming) "Healer (gaming)"), able to cast restorative and support spells; and the sprite casts offensive magic to damage and impair enemies.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-vc_ign-5) Upon collecting enough [experience points](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Experience_point "Experience point") in battle, each character increases in level and improves in areas such as strength and evasion. The trio can rest in towns, where they can regain [hit points](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Health_(gaming) "Health (gaming)") or purchase restorative items and equipment. Options such as changing equipment, casting [spells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magic_(gaming) "Magic (gaming)"), or checking status are performed by cycling through the game's Ring Commands, a [circular menu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pie_menu "Pie menu") which hovers over the currently controlled party member.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-RPGamer-3)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-NPower_1-4)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-vc_ign-5) The game is momentarily paused whenever the Ring Commands appear.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-RPGFan2-6)

Combat takes place in real-time.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-RPGamer-3) Located at the bottom of the screen is a power bar,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-DDbook-7)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-RGseries-8) a gauge that determines the amount of damage done to an enemy when attacking. Swinging a weapon causes the gauge to empty and then quickly recharge, allowing that character to attack at full strength. The party wields eight different types of weaponry: sword, spear, bow, axe, boomerang, glove, whip, and javelin. All weapons can be upgraded eight times, and repeated use of a weapon increases its skill level to a maximum of eight, unlocking a new special attack with each level. Weapons are upgraded with Weapon Orbs, which are found in [dungeons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungeon_crawl "Dungeon crawl") or earned by defeating certain [bosses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boss_(video_gaming) "Boss (video gaming)").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-RPGamer-3) The player takes each Orb to a [blacksmith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blacksmith "Blacksmith"), located in most towns, who uses it to reforge one weapon.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-RPGFan-2)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-NPower_2-9)

In order to learn magic, the party must rescue spirits known as Elementals. The eight Elementals represent different elements—such as water, earth, and life—and each provides the player with specific spells. Magic has skill levels similar to weapons, but each magic spell costs [magic points](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magic_point "Magic point") to cast.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-RPGFan-2)

At the start of the game, to reach a destination, players must traverse an enemy-infested countryside. Travel may be expedited with Cannon Travel Centers, where the party may be [launched](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_cannonball "Human cannonball") to faraway destinations via a giant [cannon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cannon "Cannon"). Cannon Travel usually requires a fee, but is mandatory to visit other continents later on.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-NPower_1-4) Later, the party is given access to Flammie, a miniature dragon which is controlled by the player and able to fly freely across the world, represented by an [overworld](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overworld "Overworld") map.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-NPower_3-10) These sequences make use of the SNES's [Mode 7](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mode_7 "Mode 7") capability to create a rotatable background, giving the illusion that the ground beneath Flammie is rendered in [three dimensions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/3D_computer_graphics "3D computer graphics"). While riding Flammie, the player may access either the "rotated map", which presents the world as a globe, or the "world map", a two-dimensional view of the overworld.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-NWRflammie-11)

## Plot

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Secret_of_Mana&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Plot")]

### Setting and characters

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Secret_of_Mana&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Setting and characters")]

The story takes place in a [high fantasy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High_fantasy "High fantasy") world, which contains an ethereal energy source named "[mana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mana_(Oceanian_mythology) "Mana (Oceanian mythology)")". An ancient, technologically advanced civilization exploited mana to construct the "Mana Fortress", a flying warship. This angered the world's gods, who sent giant beasts to war with the civilization. The conflict was globally destructive and nearly exhausted all signs of mana in the world, until a hero used the power of the Mana Sword to destroy the fortress and the civilization. The world began to recover in peace. As the game opens, an empire seeks eight Mana Seeds, which when "unsealed" will restore mana to the world and allow the empire to restore the Mana Fortress.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-backstory-12)

The three main characters do not have names in the original SNES release, though their names appear in the manual of the Japanese release; their names were added into the game in the mobile ports. In all versions, the player can choose to name the characters whatever they wish. The hero (ランディ, _Randi_),[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-chara-13) a young boy, is adopted by the Elder of Potos before the start of the game, after the boy's mother disappears. The girl (プリム, _Primm_)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-chara-13) is in love with a warrior named Dyluck, who was ordered by the king to attack Elinee's Castle. Angered by the king's actions and by her father's attempt to [arrange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arranged_marriage "Arranged marriage") her marriage to a local nobleman, she leaves the castle to save Dyluck and to accompany the hero as well.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-quoteprimm-14) The hero meets a sprite child (ポポイ, _Popoi_)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-chara-13) at the Dwarf Village. The sprite lives with a dwarf and goes with the characters to learn more about their family. It does not remember anything about its past, so it joins the team to try to recover its memories.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-quotesprite-15)

### Story

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Secret_of_Mana&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Story")]

The game begins as three boys from the small Potos village disobey their Elder's instructions and trespass into a local waterfall, where a treasure is said to be kept. One of the boys stumbles and falls into the lake, where he finds a rusty sword embedded in a stone. Guided by a disembodied voice, he pulls the sword free, inadvertently unleashing monsters in the surrounding countryside of the village. The villagers interpret the sword's removal as a bad omen and banish the boy from Potos forever.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-quotepotos-16) A traveling knight named Jema recognizes the blade as the legendary Mana Sword and encourages the hero to re-energize it by visiting the eight Mana Temples.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-quotesword-17)

During his journey, the hero is joined by the girl and the sprite. Throughout their travels, the trio is pursued by the Empire. The Emperor and his subordinates are being manipulated by Thanatos, an ancient sorcerer who hopes to create a "new, peaceful world".[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-quote1-18) Due to his own body's deterioration, Thanatos is in need of a suitable body to [possess](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spirit_possession "Spirit possession"). After placing the entire kingdom of Pandora under a trance, he abducts two candidates: Dyluck, now enslaved, and a young Pandoran girl named Phanna; he eventually chooses to possess Dyluck.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-quote2-19)

The Empire succeeds in unsealing all eight Mana Seeds. Thanatos, however, betrays the Emperor and his henchmen, killing them and seizing control of the Mana Fortress for himself. The hero and his party journey to locate the Mana Tree, the focal point of the world's life energy. Anticipating their arrival, Thanatos positions the Mana Fortress over the Tree and destroys it. The charred remains of the Tree speak to the heroes, explaining that a giant dragon called the Mana Beast will soon be summoned to combat the Fortress. The Beast has little control over its rage and will likely destroy the world as well.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-quote3-20) The Mana Tree also reveals that it was once the human wife of Serin, the original Mana Knight and the hero's father. The voice heard at Potos' waterfall was that of Serin's ghost.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-quote4-21)

The trio flies to the Mana Fortress and confronts Thanatos, who is preparing to transfer his mind into Dyluck. With the last of his strength, Dyluck warns that Thanatos has sold his soul to the [underworld](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Underworld "Underworld") and must not be allowed to have the Fortress.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-quote5-22) Dyluck kills himself, forcing Thanatos to revert to a skeletal [lich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lich "Lich") form, which the party defeats.

The Mana Beast finally flies in and attacks the Fortress. The hero expresses reluctance to kill the Beast, fearing that with the dispersal of Mana from the world, the sprite will vanish.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-quote6-23) With the sprite's encouragement, he uses the fully energized Mana Sword to slay the Beast, causing it to explode and transform into snow.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-quoteend-24) At the conclusion of the game, the sprite child vanishes into an astral plane, the girl is returned home, and the hero is seen welcomed back in Potos, returning the Mana Sword to its place beneath the waterfall.

## Development

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Secret_of_Mana&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Development")]

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f4/HiromichiTanaka20070131.jpg/250px-HiromichiTanaka20070131.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:HiromichiTanaka20070131.jpg)

_Secret of Mana_ writer and producer Hiromichi Tanaka

_Secret of Mana_ was directed and designed by Koichi Ishii, the creator of the game's [Game Boy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_Boy "Game Boy") predecessor, _[Final Fantasy Adventure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Final\_Fantasy\_Adventure "Final Fantasy Adventure")_. He has stated that he feels _Secret of Mana_ is more "his game" than other projects he has worked on, such as the _[Final Fantasy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Final\_Fantasy "Final Fantasy")_ series.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-LEVELint-25) The game was programmed primarily by [Nasir Gebelli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nasir_Gebelli "Nasir Gebelli") and produced by veteran Square designer [Hiromichi Tanaka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hiromichi_Tanaka "Hiromichi Tanaka"). The team hoped to build on the foundation of _Final Fantasy Adventure_, and they included several modified elements from that game and from other popular [Square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Square_(video_game_company) "Square (video game company)") titles in _Secret of Mana_. In addition to having better graphics and sound quality than its predecessor, the attack power gauge was changed to be more engaging, and the weapon leveling system replaced _Final Fantasy Adventure_'s system of leveling up the speed of the attack gauge.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-RGseries-8) The party system also received an upgrade from the first _Mana_ game: instead of temporary companions who could not be upgraded, party members became permanent protagonists and could be controlled by other players.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-RGseries-8) The multiplayer component was not a part of the original design, but was added when the developers realized that they could easily make all three characters human-controlled.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-LEVELint-25)

The real-time battle system used in _Secret of Mana_ has been described by its creators as an extension of the battle system used in the first three flagship _Final Fantasy_ titles. The system for experience points and leveling up was taken from _[Final Fantasy III](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Final\_Fantasy\_III "Final Fantasy III")_.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-tables-26) According to Tanaka, the game's battle system features mechanics that had first been considered for _[Final Fantasy IV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Final\_Fantasy\_IV "Final Fantasy IV")_. Similarly, unused features in _Secret of Mana_ were appropriated by the _[Chrono Trigger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrono\_Trigger "Chrono Trigger")_ team, which (like _Final Fantasy IV_) was in production at the time.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-LEVELint-25) According to Tanaka, the project was originally intended to be _Final Fantasy IV_, with a "more action-based, dynamic overworld". It "wound up not being" _Final Fantasy IV_ anymore, and instead became a separate project codenamed "_Chrono Trigger_" during development, before finally becoming _Seiken Densetsu 2_. Tanaka said that it "always felt like a sequel" to _Final Fantasy III_ for him.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-FF3-2-27)

_Secret of Mana_ was originally planned to be a launch title for the [SNES-CD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SNES-CD "SNES-CD") add-on.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-Release-28)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-SoM_Escapist-29) After the contract between [Nintendo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nintendo "Nintendo") and [Sony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony "Sony") to produce the add-on failed, and Sony repurposed its work on the SNES-CD into the competing [PlayStation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_(console) "PlayStation (console)") console, Square adapted the game for the SNES [cartridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ROM_cartridge "ROM cartridge") format. The game had to be altered to fit the storage space of a SNES game cartridge, which is much smaller than that of a CD-ROM.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-1up-30) The developers initially resisted continuing the project without the CD add-on, believing that too much of the game would have to be cut, but they were overruled by company management. As a result of the hardware change, several features had to be cut from the game, and some completed work needed to be redone.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-LEVELint-25)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-SoM_Escapist-29) One of the most significant changes was the removal of the option to take [multiple routes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nonlinear_gameplay "Nonlinear gameplay") through the game that led to several possible endings, in contrast to the linear journey in the final product.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-RGseries-8) The plot that remained was different from the original conception, and Tanaka has said that the original story had a much darker tone.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-LEVELint-25) Ishii has estimated that up to forty percent of the planned game was dropped to meet the space limitations, and critics have suggested that the hardware change led to technical problems when too much happens at once in the game.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-LEVELint-25)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-EDGEretro-31)

### Music

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Secret_of_Mana&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Music")]

Main article: [Music of the Mana series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_of_the_Mana_series "Music of the Mana series")

[![Image 9](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/8/8f/Hiroki_Kikuta.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail_unscaled)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Hiroki_Kikuta.jpg)

_Secret of Mana_ composer Hiroki Kikuta

The original score for _Secret of Mana_ was composed and produced by [Hiroki Kikuta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hiroki_Kikuta "Hiroki Kikuta"). [Kenji Ito](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenji_Ito_(composer) "Kenji Ito (composer)"), who had composed the soundtrack for _Final Fantasy Adventure_, was originally slated for the project, but was replaced with Kikuta after he had started on other projects, such as _[Romancing SaGa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romancing\_SaGa "Romancing SaGa")_. _Secret of Mana_ was Kikuta's first video game score, and he encountered difficulties in dealing with the hardware limitations of the Super NES. Kikuta tried to express in the music two "contrasting styles" to create an original score which would be neither [pop music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_music "Pop music") nor standard [game music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Video_game_music "Video game music").[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-SD2liner-32) Kikuta worked on the music mostly by himself, spending nearly 24 hours a day in his office, alternating between composing and editing to create a soundtrack that would be, according to him, "immersive" and "three-dimensional".[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-kikutaint-33) Rather than having sound engineers create the samples of instruments like most game music composers of the time, Kikuta made his own samples that matched the hardware capabilities of the Super NES. These custom samples allowed him to know exactly how each piece would sound on the system's hardware, so he did not have to worry about differences between the original composition and the Super NES.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-KikShimInt-34) Kikuta stated in 2001 that he considered the score for _Secret of Mana_ his favorite creation.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-KIKUTARBint-35)

The soundtrack's music includes both "ominous" and "light-hearted" tracks, and is noted for its use of bells and "dark, solemn pianos".[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-RPGFSM-36) Kikuta's compositions for the game were partly inspired by natural landscapes, as well as music from [Bali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bali "Bali").[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-KIKUTASMint-37)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-1UPKikutaint-38) Hardware limitations made the title screen to the game slowly fade in, and Kikuta designed the title track to the game, "Fear of the Heavens", to sync up with the screen. At that time, composers rarely tried to match a game's music to its visuals. Kikuta also started the track off with a "whale noise", rather than a traditional "ping", in order to try to "more deeply connect" the player with the game from the moment it started up. Getting the sound to work with the memory limitations of the Super NES was a difficult technical challenge.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-KikShimInt-34)

An official soundtrack album, _Seiken Densetsu 2 Original Sound Version_, was released in Japan in August 1993, containing 44 musical tracks from the game. An English version, identical to the Japanese original aside from its localized packaging and track titles, was later released in North America in December 1994 as _Secret of Mana Original Soundtrack_, making _Secret of Mana_ one of the first Japanese games to inspire a localized soundtrack release outside of Japan.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-RPGFSM-36) An album of arranged music from _Secret of Mana_ and its sequel _[Seiken Densetsu 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seiken\_Densetsu\_3 "Seiken Densetsu 3")_ was produced in 1993 as _Secret of Mana+_. The music in the album was all composed and arranged by Kikuta. _Secret of Mana+_ contains a single track, titled "Secret of Mana", that incorporates themes from the music of both _Secret of Mana_ and _Seiken Densetsu 3_, which was still under development at the time.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-SEMOSMP-39) The style of the album has been described by critics as "experimental", using "strange sounds" such as waterfalls, bird calls, cell phone sounds, and "typing" sounds.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-RPGFSMP-40) The music has also been described by critics as covering many different musical styles, such as "Debussian impressionist styles, his own heavy electronic and synth ideas, and even ideas of popular musicians".[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-SEMOSMP-39) The latest album of music from the game is a 2012 arranged album titled _Secret of Mana Genesis / Seiken Densetsu 2 Arrange Album_. The 16 tracks are upgraded versions of the original Super NES tracks, and Kikuta said in the [liner notes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liner_notes "Liner notes") for the album that they are "how he wanted the music to sound when he wrote it", without the limitations of the Super NES hardware. Critics such as Patrick Gann of RPGFan, however, noted that the differences were minor.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-RPGFgen-41) A rendition of the soundtrack was commissioned for the first ever [BBC Proms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_Proms "BBC Proms") gaming music concert in 2022.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-42)

## Release

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Secret_of_Mana&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Release")]

_Secret of Mana_ was announced for a release in July 1993, marketed as a "Party Action RPG".[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-FAMparty-43) It eventually came out on August 6 instead for the Japanese market.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-44) It was released later that same month in South Korea.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-GameWorld-45) The English translation for _Secret of Mana_ was completed in only 30 days, mere weeks after the Japanese release,[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-Release-28) and the North American [localization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_localization "Game localization") was initially advertised as _Final Fantasy Adventure 2_.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-FFA2-46) Critics have suggested that the translation was done hastily so that the game could be released in North America for the 1993 holiday season.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-1up-30) By October, the game was already available to the public.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-47) According to translator [Ted Woolsey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_Woolsey "Ted Woolsey"), a large portion of the game's script was cut out in the English localization due to space limitations.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-Release-28)[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-McGrath-48) To display text on the main gameplay screen, the English translation uses a [fixed-width font](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monospaced_font "Monospaced font"), which limits the amount of space available to display text. Woolsey was unhappy that he had to trim conversations to their bare essentials and that he had so little time for translation, commenting that it "nearly killed me".[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-HC101-49) The script was difficult to translate as it was presented to Woolsey in disordered groups of text, like "shuffling a novel".[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-McGrath-48) Other localizations were done in German and French. The Japanese release only named the three protagonists in the manual,[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-man28-50) while Western versions omitted the characters' names until the enhanced port for mobile devices.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-man35-51)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-chara-13) The game released in Europe on November 25, 1994.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-52)

In 1999, Square announced they would be porting _Secret of Mana_ to [Bandai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bandai "Bandai")'s handheld system [WonderSwan Color](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WonderSwan "WonderSwan") as one of nine planned games for the system.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-Wonderswan-53) No such port was ever released. The game was released on Virtual Console on the [Wii](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wii "Wii") in 2008 and on [Wii U](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wii_U "Wii U"), only in Japan, in 2013. A mobile phone port of _Secret of Mana_ was released on October 26, 2009.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-mobile-54) A port of the game for [iOS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IOS "IOS") was revealed at [E3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_Entertainment_Expo "Electronic Entertainment Expo") 2010, and released on Apple's App Store on December 21, 2010.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-iphone-55) The port fixed several bugs, and the English script was both edited and retranslated from the original Japanese.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-StP-56) The enhanced port from the iOS version was released on [Android](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Android_(OS) "Android (OS)") devices in 2014.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-Android-57) A port for the [Nintendo Switch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nintendo_Switch "Nintendo Switch") was released with ports of _Final Fantasy Adventure_ and _Trials of Mana_ as part of the _[Collection of Mana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Collection\_of\_Mana "Collection of Mana")_ on June 1, 2017, in Japan, and June 11, 2019 in the rest of the world.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-Switch-58)[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-SwitchNA-59) The game was released as one of the games included on the [Super NES Classic Edition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_NES_Classic_Edition "Super NES Classic Edition") on September 29, 2017.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-SNESclassic-60)

### 3D remake

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Secret_of_Mana&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: 3D remake")]

In August 2017, a 3D remake of the game was announced for [PlayStation 4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_4 "PlayStation 4"), [PlayStation Vita](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Vita "PlayStation Vita") and [Windows](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windows "Windows") and was released on February 15, 2018.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-3DRemake-61) The remake was developed by Q Studios for Square Enix.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-ManaQStudios-62) The project began in 2016 following positive feedback from _[Adventures of Mana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adventures\_of\_Mana "Adventures of Mana")_, a remake of the original _Mana_ game. The remake's gameplay was described as "basically the same" as the original, although it was redone using 3D graphics and some features were added for convenience such as an area map, increased game save opportunities, improved companion artificial intelligence, and voice acting. The offline multiplayer function was carried over into the different versions.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-RemakeInterviewIGN-63) The character art was redesigned by Haccan, an artist who had worked on _Adventures of Mana_.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-StaffVisions-64) Kikuta returned to supervise new arrangements of his music, bringing in a number of other composers he knew who were fans of _Secret of Mana_. He described his approach as composing an "adult" version of the original tracks. At the request of the series producer, the main theme "Angel's Fear" was recorded with a full orchestra.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-RemakeInterviewKikuta-65) The arranges included as [Yuzo Koshiro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yuzo_Koshiro "Yuzo Koshiro") and [Tsuyoshi Sekito](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tsuyoshi_Sekito "Tsuyoshi Sekito").[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-66) The soundtrack was released as an album, also titled _Secret of Mana Original Soundtrack_, shortly after the remake's release in February 2018.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-SOMremake-67)

## Reception

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Secret_of_Mana&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Reception")]

### Sales

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Secret_of_Mana&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Sales")]

The initial shipment of games in Japan sold out within days of the release date.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-EDGEpreview-68)_[Dengeki Oh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dengeki\_Oh "Dengeki Oh")_ magazine ranked it the second best-selling [video game of 1993](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1993_in_video_games "1993 in video games") in Japan, where 1.003 million units were sold that year, just below _[Street Fighter II Turbo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Street\_Fighter\_II\_Turbo "Street Fighter II Turbo")_.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-Dengeki-69) In South Korea, it was the top-selling game from November to December 1993.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-GameWorld-45)

_[Edge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edge\_(magazine) "Edge (magazine)")_ reported in November 1993 that the game was "the most widely covered game of the year in Japan" with a high number of sales, but was initially released in North America "completely un-hyped and mostly unheard of".[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-edge_mana-70) Despite this, _Secret of Mana_ went on to become the second top-selling Super NES game on the monthly US [Babbage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GameStop "GameStop")'s chart in October 1993, below only _[Mortal Kombat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mortal\_Kombat\_(1992\_video\_game) "Mortal Kombat (1992 video game)")_,[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-chart-71) with _Secret of Mana_ remaining in the US top ten SNES game charts for a year up until October 1994.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-EGMDec1994-72) It was also a success in Europe, where the game introduced many players to console role-playing games.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-RGseries-8) In the United Kingdom, it was the fourth top-selling game in November 1994, and the second top-selling SNES game that month (below _[Donkey Kong Country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donkey\_Kong\_Country "Donkey Kong Country")_).[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-CVG158-73)

According to _[Next Generation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Next\_Generation\_(magazine) "Next Generation (magazine)")_ magazine, it was surprisingly popular for a role-playing game, contributing to the genre's growing popularity in the West. _Next Generation_ reported in 1996 that the game had sold more than 500,000 copies in the United States alone.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-nextgen-74) According to Square Enix, _Secret of Mana_ had shipped 1.83 million copies worldwide as of 2003, with 1.5 million shipped in Japan and 330,000 abroad.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-SEsales04-75)

_[Electronic Gaming Monthly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic\_Gaming\_Monthly "Electronic Gaming Monthly")_ magazine's reviewers heavily praised the graphics, music, and multiplayer gameplay, saying that it had "some of the best music I've ever heard from a cartridge". They hoped that other companies would take the game's lead in adding multiplayer modes to role-playing games.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-egm-77)_[Diehard GameFan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GameFan "GameFan")_'s review of the game named the multiplayer as the game's best component, with reviewer Kelly Rickards saying that while the graphics were nice, the multiplayer "made the game".[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-DGFreview-79)_[GamePro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GamePro "GamePro")_'s review praised the graphics, plot, "first-rate gameplay" and "positively massive" world "dwarfing even _Zelda_", while stating the gameplay and multiplayer were "rough around the edges", concluding it to be "one of the finest action/RPGs" on the SNES.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-GPreview-81)_[Nintendo Power](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nintendo\_Power "Nintendo Power")_ said that it has "beautiful graphics and great depth of play" but criticized the "unnecessarily long" sword powering-up and "awkward" item selection method.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-NP-82)_[SNES Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SNES\_Force "SNES Force")_ magazine praised the game's "superb" graphics, "fantastic" sounds and "revolutionary three-player mode".[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-83)

_Secret of Mana_ was awarded Game of the Month in December 1993 and Best Role-Playing Game of 1993 by _Electronic Gaming Monthly_.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-egm-77)[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-egmbuyersguide1994-84) In its annual [Megawards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GameFan#Golden_Megawards "GameFan"), _GameFan_ awarded it Best Action/RPG (SNES).[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-GFaward-85)_GamePro_ gave it the award for [Role-Playing Game of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Game_of_the_Year_awards "List of Game of the Year awards"), ahead of _[Lufia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lufia\_&\_the\_Fortress\_of\_Doom "Lufia & the Fortress of Doom")_ and _[Shadowrun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shadowrun\_(1993\_video\_game) "Shadowrun (1993 video game)")_ as runners-up.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-GPaward-86)

_Edge_'s review said that _Secret of Mana_ was better than contemporary role-playing games _[Ys I & II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ys\_I\_&\_II "Ys I & II")_, _[The Legend of Zelda: A Link to the Past](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Legend\_of\_Zelda:\_A\_Link\_to\_the\_Past "The Legend of Zelda: A Link to the Past")_, and _[Landstalker: The Treasures of King Nole](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Landstalker:\_The\_Treasures\_of\_King\_Nole "Landstalker: The Treasures of King Nole")_. The review stated that _Secret of Mana_ "includes some of the best game design and features ever seen: simultaneous three-player action, the best combat system ever designed, the best player interface ever designed, a superb control system, and yes, some of the most engrossing and rewarding gameplay yet". They concluded that the game was one of the best action RPGs or adventure games.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-edge_mana-70) Game designer [Sandy Petersen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandy_Petersen "Sandy Petersen") reviewed the game in _[Dragon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragon\_(magazine) "Dragon (magazine)")_, and described the game as much like _[Zelda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Legend\_of\_Zelda "The Legend of Zelda")_ but with conventional role-playing game features. He predicted that the game would be regarded as a classic. Peterson concluded that _Secret of Mana_ was one of the best SNES role-playing games and that it was "a much larger game than _Zelda_, with many more types of monsters, character options, and fortresses to explore".[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-Dragon208-76)_[Nintendo Magazine System](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Official\_Nintendo\_Magazine "Official Nintendo Magazine")_ also compared it favorably with _A Link to the Past_; one reviewer stated that "even the magnificence of _Zelda III_ seems stale in comparison to the incredible features found within this refreshing, exhilarating adventure" while the other stated that it "comes the closest yet" to surpassing _Zelda_, concluding that _Secret of Mana_ was "one of the greatest graphical RPGs in the history of the world".[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-NMS-80)

_[Computer and Video Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer\_and\_Video\_Games "Computer and Video Games")_ said in 1994 that _Mana_ was "doing for adventure games now what Zelda did several years ago" and that _Mana_ is "one of the best games for the SNES this year and more playable than" _[Donkey Kong Country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donkey\_Kong\_Country "Donkey Kong Country")_.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-CVG158-73)_Next Generation_ said in 1996 that many players considered it "the RPG equivalent of _[Lord of the Rings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lord\_of\_the\_Rings "Lord of the Rings")_."[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-nextgen-74)

In 2008, Lucas Thomas of _[IGN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IGN "IGN")_ reviewed the [Virtual Console](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virtual_Console "Virtual Console") release of _Secret of Mana_ and stated that it was considered one of the best video games ever made.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-vc_ign-5)_[Eurogamer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eurogamer "Eurogamer")_'s Dan Whitehead described it as "essential" and as the formative game of the _Mana_ series.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-EUROG-90) The [iOS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IOS "IOS") version of the game was praised by Nadia Oxford of Slide to Play for its improved graphics and computer-controlled characters. She also praised the quality of the touch controls relative to other role-playing game phone versions, though she disliked that the multiplayer mode had been removed.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-StP-56) In 2014, _Edge_ magazine described _Secret of Mana_ as "one of the high points of the 16bit era". A writer for the magazine noted that, 20 years after _Secret of Mana_'s release, its reputation as a SNES action RPG had been surpassed only by that of _The Legend of Zelda: A Link to the Past_.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-EDGEretro-31)

The 2018 remake saw "mixed or average" reviews according to [review aggregation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Review_aggregator "Review aggregator") website _[Metacritic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metacritic "Metacritic")_, with the PS4 version scoring 63 out of 100 based on 60 reviews, while the PC version was scored 57 out of 100 based on six reviews.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-MetaRemake-89)_RPG Site_'s Zack Reese positively noted the attempts to modernise the gameplay while remaining faithful to the original, but felt people were better off playing the original due to its 3D presentation and lack of additional gameplay improvements.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-RPGreview2018-93) Meghan Sullvan of _IGN_ described the game as "a charming but clumsy 20ish-hour adventure that both frustrates and delights", praising the artstyle but faulting a lack of improvements over the original.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-IGNreview2018-94)_Game Informer_'s Kimberley Wallace did enjoy her time with the game but felt some of the adjustments did not improve the gameplay, further faulting poor voice acting and uneven musical remixes.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-GIreview2018-95) Jeremy Parish, writing for _Polygon_, felt the remake compared poorly to the original's recent ports on Nintendo platforms, finding issues with its 3D redesign and repetitive character conversations.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-PolyReview2018-96) Chris Schilling of _[PC Gamer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PC\_Gamer "PC Gamer")_ was particularly critical, saying the original appeared much smoother by comparison, disliking the new 3D graphics and faulting lack of noticeable adjustments to the pacing and difficulty.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-PCGreview2018-97)

### Impact

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Secret_of_Mana&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Impact")]

_Secret of Mana_ has placed on numerous top game lists since its release, and is the 13th highest-rate SNES game on aggregator website [GameRankings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GameRankings "GameRankings").[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-GameRankings-87) In 1995, _[Total!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Total! "Total!")_ rated _Secret of Mana_ 12th on their "Top 100 SNES Games of All Time,"[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-Total-98) with _[Super Play](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super\_Play "Super Play")_ ranked it eighth on its list of the best 100 SNES games of all time the following year.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-superplay-99) It has continued to be placed on "best of" lists of SNES games, games for Nintendo consoles, or role-playing ever since, including ones by _[Nintendo Power](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nintendo\_Power "Nintendo Power")_,[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-NPbestof-100)_IGN_,[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-IGNtoprpg17-101)_[Famitsu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Famitsu "Famitsu")_,[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-Famitsupoll-102)_[Official Nintendo Magazine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Official\_Nintendo\_Magazine "Official Nintendo Magazine")_,[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-ONMbestof-103)_[Game Informer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game\_Informer "Game Informer")_,[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-GIbestof-104)_[1Up.com](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1Up\_Network "1Up Network")_,[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-1UPbestof-105)_[Polygon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polygon\_(website) "Polygon (website)")_,[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-PGbestof-106) and _Time Extension_,[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-TEbestof-107) as recently as 2023.

In 2006, _Level_ magazine claimed that _Secret of Mana_'s rocky development was Square's main inspiration to move their games, such as the _Final Fantasy_ series, from Nintendo consoles to Sony consoles in 1996.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-LEVELint-25)_Secret of Mana_ was an influential game in its time, and its influence continued into the 2010s. Elements such as its radial ring menu system, described by _Edge_ as "oft-mimicked", were borrowed by later games such as _[The Temple of Elemental Evil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Temple\_of\_Elemental\_Evil\_(video\_game) "The Temple of Elemental Evil (video game)")_.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-DDbook-7)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-EDGEretro-31) Its cooperative multiplayer gameplay has been mentioned as an influence on _[Dungeon Siege III](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungeon\_Siege\_III "Dungeon Siege III")_.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_of_Mana#cite_note-NowGamer-108)
